summary:
Neoda is a free web tool that answers a simple question with 45 years of NASA data: is Spain running out of water, and where? It detects (it does not predict) statistically significant trends in 19 water-related indicators for each of Spain's 52 provinces, using NASA POWER data from 1981 to 2025.

Debates about drought and irrigation are often based on a single dry year. Neoda replaces impressions with evidence: for any province it shows how rainfall, temperature, evaporation, soil moisture and drought indices have really changed, how fast, and whether the change is significant (Mann-Kendall test, Sen's slope with confidence intervals).

A map of Spain answers plain-language questions for anyone, and an analysis panel gives scientists and water managers the full statistics and a PDF report. Key finding: since 1991 temperature rises in all 52 provinces and crop water demand in 25, while rainfall has not fallen. The pressure on water comes from heat and evaporation. The tool is bilingual, works on mobile and can scale to any region of the world.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Neoda detects (it does not predict) statistically significant trends in 19 water indicators for the 52 Spanish provinces, using NASA POWER data from 1981 to 2025. It has three views, in English and Spanish:

- Home: a short scroll story that explains the water problem in Spain, plus a 30-second demo video.

- Map of Spain: every province coloured by a plain-language question ("Where is it getting hotter?", "Where do farms need more irrigation?"), as trend per decade or average value, with a ranking. Faded colours mean the change is not significant.

- Analysis panel: pick a province (and optionally a second one to compare), the indicators, the period and the significance level. Neoda returns a verdict in plain words, a combined water index, the variables driving the change, one card per indicator and a PDF report.

HOW IT WORKS

1. The browser calls the NASA POWER monthly point API live (no key). Each province is represented by 1 to 6 land sampling points. GitHub Actions keeps a backup copy.

2. 15 indicators come directly from NASA POWER. 4 are computed: reference evapotranspiration (FAO-56 Penman-Monteith), water balance (P - ETo), aridity index (UNEP) and the SPI-12 drought index.

3. Statistics: Mann-Kendall trend test, Sen's slope with confidence interval, and linear regression with a t-test. Monthly series are de-seasonalised.

4. A combined water index (signed z-scores) shows whether water availability improves or worsens, and which variable drives the change.

5. Validated against pymannkendall, SciPy and FAO-56 Example 17. Automated tests run on every deploy.

KEY FINDING

Since 1991, temperature rises in all 52 provinces and crop water demand rises in 25, but rainfall has not fallen (it rises in 17 and falls in 1). The pressure on water in Spain comes from heat and evaporation, not from less rain.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Evidence instead of anecdotes: it separates a real trend from a single dry year. Cooperatives, municipalities and river basin authorities can see where irrigation demand rises or soils dry out. It is free, needs no account, works on mobile and can be shared as a link or a PDF. NASA POWER is global, so any region of the world can be added. Next steps: NASA GRACE (groundwater), MODIS (vegetation), Copernicus, alerts and an API.

CREATIVITY

Instead of a technical dashboard, Neoda turns statistics into plain-language questions and verdicts that a non-expert can understand. Scientists still get every number behind each answer.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Honesty about limits: satellites and reanalysis do not see desalination or groundwater pumping, the grid is about 50 km, and correlation is not causation. We flag near-constant series instead of reporting false trends. We also designed for accessibility, mobile use and two languages.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript, Plotly.js, Leaflet, jsPDF, Python (Shapely, NumPy, SciPy, pymannkendall, pytest), Node.js, GitHub Pages and GitHub Actions, Remotion (demo video).

Code: https://github.com/fpanero/Neoda_Heeramienta_Medicion

Full report (PDF): https://github.com/fpanero/Neoda_Heeramienta_Medicion/blob/main/docs/Neoda_SpaceApps2026_Report.pdf
